To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have experimentally confirmed a previously reported numerical result that shows that the emission of radiation from a soliton in a silicon wire pumped around 1550 nm can lead to supercontinuum generation spanning over 500 nm.

we have experimentally confirmed that a previously reported numerical simulation of supercontinuum generation by soliton fission and resonant radiation emission in a silicon nanowire can be realized at telecommunication wavelengths, by dispersion engineering.
a supercontinuum can be generated in silicon waveguide by using the soliton fission and resonant radiation emission mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of ultrafast silicon photonics sources for applications in optical communications.
the generation of supercontinua in the near-infrared region of the spectrum.
the study of the nonlinear optical response of a silicon wire wave guide at telecommunication wavelengths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the generation of a broad supercontinuum in silicon waveguides can be explained by soliton fission in combination with resonant emission from the dispersive waves.
the generation of supercontinuum in a silicon wire pumped around the 1.55 μm telecommunication wavelength is a result of the interaction between solitons and resonant radiation.
the supercontinuum generation is due to the dispersive wave radiation from the soliton fission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the supercontinuum generated from the soliton fission is a result of the emission of dispersive waves from the solitonic core, and that the supercontinua generated in the silicon waveguide are comparable to those generated in the photonic crystal fibers.
the supercontinuum generation can be controlled by dispersion engineering.
we experimentally confirm the numerical study of a previous work, which shows that the emission of a resonant radiation from solitons can result in the generation of supercontinuum spanning 500 nm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generation of supercontinua in the near-infrared is possible with a single pump wavelength in a silicon waveguide.
a supercontinuum can be generated in a silicon wire by pumping it around the 1552 nm telecommunication wavelength, a wavelength that is currently not used for supercontinuum generation.
the emission of dispersive waves can lead to supercontinuum generation at telecommunication wavelengths in a silicon waveguide.
